new_groups.label: Wilkes's speech in the Commons
new_groups.definition: Printings of the speech of John Wilkes, Lord Mayor of London, in the House of Commons on the motion for an address to the King at the opening of the session in October 1775, against the war in America.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Governor Penn before the Lords
new_groups.definition: Reports of the examination of Richard Penn, former governor of Pennsylvania, who had carried Congress's petition to the King, in the House of Lords in November 1775, as the American papers printed them from February 1776: a short London report, and a long account with the questions and answers. Contains those two groups; the wider coverage is not included.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A London report: Penn examined
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London paragraph of November 1775: on Friday Governor Penn was examined in the Upper Assembly and 'gave very satisfactory answers', and a member then proposed Congress's last petition to the King as the basis of an accommodation.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Lords examine Governor Penn
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London account of the House of Lords on 10 November 1775: the examination of Richard Penn, with the questions put to him and his answers, and the Duke of Richmond's motion grounded on them.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Prohibitory bill in the Commons
new_groups.definition: Reports from London of the bill to prohibit all trade and intercourse with the colonies (the Prohibitory Act) in the House of Commons in December 1775, as printed in February and March 1776: the debate in committee, which printed the clause on captures with blanks for its dates, and the clause as settled. Contains those two groups; the wider coverage is not included.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Commons in committee on the bill
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London report (6 December 1775) of the House of Commons in committee on the bill to prohibit all trade and intercourse with the colonies: the divisions, Lord North's remark on the clause that gives American ships time, and that clause printed with blanks for its dates, 'that the friends of America may have an opportunity' to have them filled with distant ones.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The clause on captures settled
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London report (8 December 1775) that the clause of the bill which caused the greatest debate was settled: American ships to be captured from 1 January 1776, and all ships trading with the colonies from 1 June 1776.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Congress on refusing Continental bills
new_groups.definition: Printings of Congress's resolution of 11 January 1776 that anyone who refused the Continental bills of credit, or discouraged their circulation, should be treated as an enemy of his country.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Congress's fast day of 17 May
new_groups.definition: Printings of Congress's resolution of 16 March 1776 recommending that Friday 17 May be kept throughout the colonies as a day of humiliation, fasting and prayer. Includes a one-sentence notice of it and a New York committee's notice that quotes it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Barry takes the Edward
new_groups.definition: Printings of Captain John Barry's letter to John Hancock or the Marine Committee ('In sight of the Capes of Virginia, April 7, 1776'): he fell in with the sloop Edward, belonging to the Liverpool frigate, and took her after a fight of near two glasses.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The sloop Liberty's gunpowder taken
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Williamsburg report (13 April 1776) that on 30 March the sloop Liberty of Perth Amboy, from St. Eustatius with 83 barrels of gunpowder, dry goods and medicines, was taken by a British tender off the capes and carried into Norfolk, with what her mate, who escaped, said of British troops at Antigua.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Howe brothers' declarations
new_groups.definition: The declarations of Lord Howe and General William Howe as the King's commissioners for restoring peace, as the American papers printed them: Lord Howe's declaration of June 1776, published by order of Congress in July, and the brothers' declaration of 19 September. Contains those two groups; their declaration of 14 July (printed in the New-York Gazette) and their proclamation of 30 November (printed in the Freeman's Journal) are not included.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Lord Howe's declaration, published by Congress
new_groups.definition: Printings of Congress's resolution of 19 July 1776 ordering that Lord Howe's circular letter to the former royal governors (20 June 1776) and the declaration it enclosed be published, 'that the good people of these United States may be informed of what nature are the Commissioners, and what the terms', followed by the letter and the declaration offering pardons.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The declaration of 19 September
new_groups.definition: Printings of the declaration of Lord Howe and General William Howe, the King's commissioners, of 19 September 1776: Congress had disavowed every purpose of reconciliation, the King would revise his instructions and the acts complained of, and the inhabitants were invited to consider whether to trust their fate to Congress.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Gates on Carleton's retreat
new_groups.definition: Printings of General Gates's letter to the President of Congress (Ticonderoga, 5 November 1776), published by order of Congress, reporting that General Carleton's fleet and army had withdrawn from Crown Point.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1776 printings, checked against the scan.

dispositions_summary.method: Round two took the ten candidates that round one read but did not admit (each counted by the item finder in 7 or 8 newspapers), leaving out the reports of Cherokee and Creek plans, which need careful framing first. Each candidate's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 2,319 pages of 1776 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched by hand for garbled printings; none was found. Nine stories were admitted (15 groups, 87 printings); one candidate was not.
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one, a story is admitted when it reaches 7 or more newspapers, and printings are counted item by item. Where a candidate turned out to be two related printed items, each item is its own group under a parent story, as in round one; in this round such a sub-story can reach fewer than 7 papers (the Commons committee report on the Prohibitory bill, 6; the settled clause, 5; the Howes' declaration of 19 September, 6). A paper that printed an item again later counts each printing.

candidates_split.The Commons debate on the Prohibitory bi: two London reports joined by the clause on captures: the committee debate of 5 December 1775 with the clause printed with blanks for its dates (6 papers), and the clause as settled on 8 December (5 papers). Admitted as two groups under a parent story.
candidates_split.Governor Penn examined in the Lords: two London items: a short report that Penn was examined (7 papers) and the long account of the examination with questions and answers (8 papers). Admitted as two groups under a parent story.
candidates_split.Congress on refusing Continental bills (: Congress's resolution of 11 January 1776 (7 papers) is admitted. The other printings are not one notice repeated: they are separate notices of committees of inspection, which quote the resolution and then name people found to have refused the bills (see not_admitted).
candidates_split.The Howe brothers' declarations (item fi: several documents with the same heading: Lord Howe's declaration of June 1776 published by Congress in July (7 papers) and the brothers' declaration of 19 September (6 papers) are admitted as two groups under a parent story; the rest are listed in not_admitted.
